niche: a retailer-owned cooperative grocery wholesaler sizing which inbound suppliers to move from delivered prices to collected (ex-works) prices, collected by its own store-delivery trucks on their empty return legs
answer: Move Meagher Dairies, Colleneler Preserves, Devanney Fresh Foods, Kenlan Meats, O'Kieve Crisps, Briody Grain Foods and Paten Flour Mills onto collected terms from 1 March 2027, saving EUR 370,900 a year (370,890.45 unrounded); the eleven that pay alone (EUR 503,400) double-book four corridors' return trips.
answer_source: task106/submission.md, Final Recommendation; task106/golden/collected_terms_2027.xlsx, first sheet
stakeholder_role: head of buying terms at a cooperative grocery wholesaler

spine.entity: one store delivery trip (route-day) with its stops and its return leg
spine.source: synthetic (fictional cooperative's transport management export); real Irish towns, real Irish public holidays, EU drivers' hours rules (Regulation (EC) No 561/2006)

world.org_type: retailer-owned cooperative grocery wholesaler serving independent convenience stores

driver: The decisive quantity is what a set of candidates can jointly realise when each one draws on a shared, finite pool of spare capacity, so sizing every candidate against the whole pool and adding them up overstates the set and admits members whose share of the pool is already taken by better ones; a pilot whose members never shared the pool reproduces exactly under the independent sizing and cannot see it.
driver_concrete: A supplier's collection saving is earned only on a store truck's return leg that passes it with enough spare driving time for the detour, and suppliers on the same corridor draw on the same few return legs, so netting each supplier's allowance against every leg that passes it and switching all that pay double-books the corridor legs; the 2026 pilot ran one supplier per corridor, so it reproduces the independent sizing to the cent.
stump: A competent solver nets each supplier's collection allowance of the detour cost on the return legs that pass it and can take its orders, switches every supplier that still pays, and files that set and its annual saving; it never lets the switched suppliers compete for the same return legs, so it double-books the busiest corridor's legs, overstates the saving and switches suppliers whose legs a better supplier already uses.

differentiation.task64: task64 allocates a cross-partition supply shortfall by a rule recovered from refused orders; task106 has no recovered allocation rule, the shared pool is spare driving time on return legs and the decision is which members join the set at all
differentiation.task69: task69's slate members overlap in the events they cover; task106's members cover disjoint volume and compete for a capacity pool, so the overstatement comes from double-booked legs rather than double-counted events
differentiation.task32: task32 v3 is a single filed annual by-product cap that rules out the tier a forecast covers; task106 has no filed cap on the answer, the limit is trailer room left after returns on each return trip, and it binds pairwise between candidates competing for the same trips.
differentiation.task36: task36 R4 to R5 excludes the largest repair by a filed rule (a counterparty agreement already remedies it) and rescopes a population through a join; task106 excludes no candidate by rule, the losers pay on their own and lose only because a better supplier takes the same return trips.
differentiation.task37: task37's wage class ask is an eligibility condition on a rate-anchored determination that changes which of four classes is certified; task106 has no eligibility condition, every candidate is eligible and the set is an optimum over shared trip capacity.
differentiation.task43: task43 iteration B allocates a fixed number of places to the units an intervention moves, found through a moderator behind a directory join; task106 has no count cap, the capacity is per trip and per day, and which supplier keeps a trip is decided by the subset optimum, not by a moderator.
differentiation.task50: task50 v4 measures how much of each candidate's exposure falls inside a funded window by projecting a filed issue order forward; task106 has no window containment or queue projection, it nets each supplier's allowance against detours and resolves who shares return trips.
differentiation.task57: task57 v21 and v22 bind a grant line on filed place limits per band, summing the lesser of places and population; task106 has no per-band place limit, the room is spare trailer space on each return trip and candidates exclude each other pairwise.
differentiation.task58: task58 v8 sizes the smallest supplement under a capped pro-rata formula and v15 floors entitlements at the sub-unit grain after a split; task106 has no pro-rata formula, floor or partition, it picks which candidates join a set when two cannot share one return trip.
differentiation.task73: task73 world ten fits a capped slate under a monthly processing allocation whose forward load comes from re-assigning review intervals; task106 has no forward load to re-derive, the room on each return trip is observed, and the binding fact is that two switched orders never fit one trip.
differentiation.task76: task76 v1 caps an open run with a rolling per-unit entitlement ceiling consumed through a second payment channel; task106 has no per-unit ceiling or second channel, every supplier's saving stands alone and is lost only to a competitor for the same trips.
differentiation.task79: task79 solves a piecewise inverse against a capacity constant recovered as the closed periods' maximum; task106 recovers no constant, trip room is filed (fleet spaces less returns), and the decision is a subset of candidates rather than a required input volume.
differentiation.task87: task87 v2 binds a per-entity cumulative cap where entity membership is constructed from shared identifiers; task106 has no entity grouping or cumulative cap, each supplier is its own candidate and the capacity is one order per return trip.
